title: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
subtitle: Italian-American polpette in slow-cooked tomato sauce
excerpt: The ultimate comfort food: tender beef and pork meatballs, pan-fried until crusted, then simmered low and slow in a simple, deeply flavoured tomato sauce until both the meatballs and the sauce have enriched each other. Serve over pasta or with bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Polpette (meatballs) are eaten across Italy but the version simmered in tomato sauce and served over spaghetti is predominantly an Italian-American creation, shaped by the immigrant experience in New York from the late nineteenth century onwards. In Italy, meatballs are often smaller, fried, and eaten as a contorno (side dish) or in broth; the large meatball in rich tomato sauce over pasta is the diaspora's version, influenced by the abundance of meat and pasta available in America. A mix of beef and pork produces a lighter, moister meatball than pure beef; the addition of soaked bread (panade) keeps them tender and stops them becoming dense. The sauce should cook slowly to develop sweetness from the tomatoes.

content.text: Soak the breadcrumbs in milk first: the soaked bread (panade) keeps the meatballs moist and tender. Do not overwork the mixture after adding the bread or they will become dense and tough. Brown them in batches without crowding; the crust adds flavour to the final sauce.

items.preparation: soaked in 4 tbsp whole milk for 5 minutes
2 for the meatballs; 1 for the sauce

content.text: Mix together the beef mince, pork mince, soaked breadcrumbs (squeeze out most of the milk first), egg, parmesan, 2 grated garlic cloves, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix with your hands until just combined; do not overwork. With wet hands, form into balls about 4 cm in diameter.

Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the meatballs in batches without touching them for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until deeply browned on two sides. Remove and set aside. Reduce the heat. Cook the onion in the pan for 6 minutes until soft. Add the remaining garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes, oregano, and bay leaves. Stir, scraping up the browned bits. Return the meatballs to the sauce. Partially cover and simmer over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, turning the meatballs once, until they are cooked through and the sauce is thick. Remove the bay leaves. Serve over pasta or with crusty bread.
